title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment. A camera network built to support police work was queried by an officer who had a personal connection to the person he was looking up. The searches ran through the Flock system and through CJIS and CORI, which are restricted state and criminal justice databases. The misuse happened at the point of lookup, not in the camera hardware or the matching software, and it repeated across 2024 and 2025.

What would have caught it is auditing of who queried whom and why. The searches were tied to a named officer and a named subject, so a review that compared query logs against case assignments could have flagged the pattern. The department's own internal affairs investigation did establish that he used state systems to obtain information about the woman, and a criminal complaint followed. The gap was detection at the time of the query rather than months later.

It is not established that Rogers is guilty of any crime, and the criminal complaint is an accusation rather than a finding. The internal affairs conclusion covers the use of the systems, not the intent behind it, and the Select Board has not yet decided his employment status.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the relationship about five years ago, changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits after leaving. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 for potential state law violations. After a four-week internal affairs investigation, the department found he used state systems to obtain information about the woman. Rogers was placed on paid administrative leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has a restraining order lasting at least a year. A Select Board hearing next week could decide Rogers' employment status.
